john-kiriakou.body_append:
## News consumption habits (Consortium News 30th)

At [Consortium News](/wiki/consortium-news)'s 30th-anniversary panel in November 2025, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said he *"defaults to the written word"* and cannot watch most video news, offering a standing insult for the format: *"any slob can roll out of bed and make a YouTube video — you live in your parents' basement, you wake up in the morning, you roll out of bed, you eat some Doritos, and then you put on a news show on YouTube."*<Cite t="1:26:34" /><Cite t="1:27:06" /> He said he has, over the years, curated his X and Blue Sky feeds around a dozen or so writers whose judgment he trusts — naming Patrick Lawrence, [Ray McGovern](/wiki/ray-mcgovern), Mary Kostakidis and Joe Lauria — and now gets *"most of my news"* from those platforms rather than from television or written mainstream press, defending his continued use of X against friends who criticise him for it on the grounds that *"so long as the people whose judgment I trust are able to publish on these platforms, I'll seek them out on those platforms."*<Cite t="1:27:36" /><Cite t="1:28:09" />

tucker-carlson.body_append:
## 'Genuinely worried' about being cancelled (2025)

At the [Consortium News](/wiki/consortium-news) 30th-anniversary panel in November 2025, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said [Tucker Carlson](/wiki/tucker-carlson) *"genuinely is worried"* about being cancelled or targeted over his independent-media output, and that the worry is *"new"* for Carlson personally — whereas the friend Kiriakou also cites, Judge Andrew Napolitano, has been living with the same worry for five years. Kiriakou linked the shift to a public break the same day between [Donald Trump](/wiki/donald-trump) and Marjorie Taylor Greene, in which Trump publicly *"called her a traitor and withdrew his political endorsement of her."*<Cite t="2:01:40" /><Cite t="2:02:11" /><Cite t="2:02:43" />

ray-mcgovern.body_append:
## In Kiriakou's trusted-feed cohort (2025)

[John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) named [Ray McGovern](/wiki/ray-mcgovern) at the [Consortium News](/wiki/consortium-news) 30th-anniversary panel in November 2025 as one of the small handful of writers whose feeds he checks daily on X and Blue Sky for news — the same short list on which he placed Patrick Lawrence, Mary Kostakidis and Joe Lauria — as the mechanism by which he now escapes what he calls the intolerable ecosystem of *"any slob"* rolling out of bed to make a YouTube show.<Cite t="1:27:36" /><Cite t="1:28:09" />

consortium-news.body_append:
## 30th-anniversary panel (November 2025)

On 15 November 2025 [Consortium News](/wiki/consortium-news) marked its thirtieth birthday with a live panel featuring editor Joe Lauria in Washington, executive producer Kathy Vogans in Sydney, Elizabeth Vos in Arkansas and columnists Mary Kostakidis, Patrick Lawrence, [Ray McGovern](/wiki/ray-mcgovern) and [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou).<Cite t="11:34" /> Kiriakou used his contributions to argue that the outlet's continuing role is to publish a small stable of writers — Patrick Lawrence, McGovern, Kostakidis and Lauria — whose judgment can substitute for the video news he refuses to consume, and to defend the survival of independent outlets by way of curated distribution through X and Blue Sky where those writers can still be found.<Cite t="1:26:34" /><Cite t="1:27:36" /><Cite t="1:28:09" />
